theory.intro: Use the inverse to reverse a calculation or compare the two reflected graphs.
facts: For an increasing one-to-one function, any intersection with its inverse lies on $y=x$.
A decreasing function can meet its inverse away from $y=x$; check the actual graphs or compositions.
A self-inverse function satisfies $f(f(x))=x$ on its domain.

foundation.solution_text:
$f(f(x))=a^2x+5(a+1)$
For this to equal $x$ for all inputs, $a^2=1$ and $a+1=0$.
$a=-1$

foundation.question_text:
A conversion uses $f(x)=8x-6$.
Find the input that gives output $26$.

A conversion uses $f(x)=3x-1$.
Find the input that gives output $11$.

foundation.solution_text:
$f^{-1}(x)=x-2$
The lines have the same gradient and different intercepts.
$\text{no intersections}$
